title: China’s Quiet Bet on Methanol Is Paying Off
gist: A 1995 Ford–China methanol vehicle collaboration that Ford abandoned in 1998 survived in China through provincial coalitions, and Geely’s Farizon now sells more than 10,000 methanol trucks and buses a year with running costs 20–40 percent below diesel; the July 2026 Ford–Geely joint venture at Ford’s Valencia plant inverts the original technology-transfer direction and illustrates the payoff of industrial policy that preserves multiple technological pathways rather than picking a winner.

insights.claim: Technology leadership depends less on the technology itself than on whether governments, firms, and local institutions are willing to sustain multiple technological pathways long enough for one of them to mature.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Use pathway breadth, not current commercial viability, as the metric when assessing which national industrial programs will produce winners a decade out.
insights.locator: Tech leadership, especially in Big Tech forms of innovation

insights.claim: Technologies should not be judged solely on current commercial viability because engineering advances can fundamentally reshape cost structures, infrastructure requirements, and the role a technology plays in a broader energy system.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Written-off technologies with active engineering programs are where asymmetric returns hide — methanol is the worked example.
insights.locator: Yet this evolution illustrates an important principle

insights.claim: China’s industrial policy in this story as in many others produced duplication, overinvestment, failures, and corruption — the acknowledged cost of preserving technological options.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: The optionality thesis is not a free lunch; waste is the premium paid for the option, which matters when scoring Chinese capital efficiency.
insights.locator: China’s industrial policy has also produced duplication

insights.claim: China prioritized battery EVs but rarely relied on a single technological pathway, letting battery EVs, fuel cells, plug-in hybrids, and methanol develop simultaneously under different regional conditions rather than forcing an immediate winner.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: China’s powertrain portfolio is broader than the EV headline suggests — Western competitors betting on a single pathway carry more technology risk.
insights.locator: China’s approach was also more technologically inclusive

insights.claim: Ford ended methanol development around 1998 after U.S. oil companies largely stopped expanding public methanol fueling infrastructure, and redirected to ethanol, which had stronger political support and a more favorable agricultural coalition in the United States and Brazil.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Fueling infrastructure and lobby coalitions, not engineering merit, decided the U.S. alternative-fuel winner — the same dynamic now governs hydrogen and charging buildouts.

insights.claim: Rising natural gas prices, falling oil prices, and concerns over methanol’s toxicity and corrosiveness further weakened the business case in the United States.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Methanol economics are levered to the gas-to-oil price spread — a relationship that has flipped as renewable-powered production emerged.
insights.locator: Rising natural gas prices, falling oil prices

insights.claim: Methanol has real technical drawbacks: lower energy density than gasoline requiring larger tanks for the same range, engine corrosion, and poor cold-start performance.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: These are the engineering problems Geely spent years solving — the moat is in the fixes, not the fuel.
insights.locator: Yet methanol has faced significant technical and commercial challenges

insights.claim: No comparable coalition of state governments, firms, and sustained federal industrial policy emerged in the United States to commercialize methanol long-term, even though energy firms and researchers periodically argued it could create opportunities for historically coal-dependent states.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Subnational industrial coalitions are the missing U.S. institution — a structural explanation for repeated American failures to commercialize domestically invented technologies.
insights.locator: The contrast with the United States is instructive

insights.claim: Since 2019 Geely’s commercial vehicle subsidiary Farizon has manufactured and sold more than 10,000 methanol-powered trucks and buses annually, giving China one of the world’s largest methanol commercial vehicle fleets.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: This is a real commercial business, not a pilot — a data point for anyone modeling Chinese heavy-duty decarbonization beyond battery trucks.
insights.locator: Since 2019, Geely’s commercial vehicle subsidiary Farizon

insights.claim: Chinese methanol commercial vehicles deliver power output comparable to diesel counterparts with cleaner emissions, similar upfront purchase costs, and running costs that are 20 to 40 percent lower.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: A 20–40 percent opex advantage at parity capex is the kind of TCO gap that flips fleet purchasing decisions — a threat to diesel powertrain suppliers in coal-producing regions.
insights.locator: These methanol vehicles deliver power output comparable

insights.claim: Geely’s methanol vehicles either use methanol-fueled internal combustion engines as primary power or employ methanol-powered range extenders to recharge onboard batteries, a hybrid architecture that avoids charging-infrastructure dependence.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Range-extender architectures let Chinese OEMs monetize electrification in regions where charging density is poor — a template for emerging-market exports.
insights.locator: These vehicles either use methanol-fueled internal combustion engines

insights.claim: Geely recognized in 2005 that methanol vehicles could serve industrial development, energy security, cleaner transport, and demand for local coal at once, then spent years fixing corrosion, cold starts, durability, and safety.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: A twenty-year single-firm engineering commitment is what turned a dead technology into a product — the timescale Western capital allocation rarely tolerates.
insights.locator: Geely emerged as the most important corporate backer

insights.claim: Geely’s methanol program was sustained not by national policy alone but by a coalition of provincial governments including Shanxi, Guizhou, Henan, and Sichuan that provided operational subsidies, public bus fleet replacement, incentives for methanol commercial vehicles, and fueling infrastructure investment.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Reading Chinese industrial policy only at the national level misses where the demand actually gets created — provincial budgets are the operative variable.
insights.locator: Provincial governments helped create a market

insights.claim: Chinese local governments were not merely implementing national strategy but were active participants in shaping the technological trajectory of the methanol vehicle industry.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Treat provincial policy divergence as a leading indicator of which Chinese technologies scale — the center often ratifies rather than initiates.
insights.locator: In this sense, local governments were not merely implementing

insights.claim: For coal-producing provinces seeking industrial upgrading, methanol offered a way to convert an existing resource advantage into a new industrial ecosystem linking coal, clean fuels, advanced vehicle manufacturing, and energy security.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: The coal-to-methanol-to-vehicles chain is a resource-region industrial upgrade template with obvious analogues in other coal economies.
insights.locator: For coal-producing provinces seeking industrial upgrading

insights.claim: The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology launched a nationwide methanol vehicle pilot program across several coal- and methanol-producing provinces in 2012, around the same time China launched its celebrated “Ten Cities, Thousand Vehicles” EV demonstration program.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
entities: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
insights.so_what: The methanol pilot ran in parallel with the famous EV program for fourteen years — evidence the multi-pathway strategy was deliberate, not accidental.

insights.claim: China formally incorporated methanol-powered shipping and green-methanol production into its green-transition policy framework in 2024, and the 15th Five-Year Plan for 2026-30 calls for further development of methanol fueling infrastructure and industrial ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Five-Year-Plan backing signals sustained Chinese demand for green methanol capacity — relevant to marine fuel, electrolyzer, and carbon-capture supply chains.
insights.locator: In 2024, China formally incorporated methanol-powered shipping

insights.claim: The rapid decline in wind and solar costs has opened new possibilities for methanol production, with renewable electricity making low-cost hydrogen via electrolysis that can react with captured carbon dioxide to synthesize methanol.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Cheap renewables convert methanol from a coal derivative into a green fuel — the economics that justify the marine and heavy-transport buildout.
insights.locator: The rapid decline in the cost of wind and solar power

insights.claim: Methanol is increasingly viewed not simply as an alternative transport fuel but as an efficient carrier of hydrogen, offering a pathway that addresses hydrogen storage and transportation challenges while contributing to carbon capture and utilization.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: If methanol wins as the hydrogen carrier, liquid-hydrogen and ammonia infrastructure bets lose — a live fork in the energy-transition supply chain.
insights.locator: Increasingly, methanol is being viewed not simply as an alternative

insights.claim: Methanol’s appeal for energy security rests on producibility from a wide range of feedstocks from coal to biomass and on the fact that existing gasoline engines can be modified to run on methanol blends or pure methanol.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Feedstock flexibility plus retrofittable engines means methanol can scale without a new vehicle fleet — the lowest-capex decarbonization path for legacy ICE stock.
insights.locator: Methanol is a relatively convenient alternative fuel

themes.theme: Ford-Geely Valencia and the Reversed Flow of Know-How

insights.claim: Ford and Geely announced in July plans for a Europe-focused joint venture at Ford’s Valencia plant in Spain, owned two-thirds by Ford and one-third by Geely, producing three Ford-branded multi-energy vehicles and two Geely electric models beginning in 2028.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: A concrete 2028 production start with defined equity split — the template for how Chinese OEM technology enters Europe without a greenfield plant.

insights.claim: The Ford-Geely arrangement reverses the 1990s roles: Ford once brought technological and engineering expertise to China seeking market access, while today Geely brings vehicle technologies, manufacturing efficiency, and sophisticated supply chains and Ford contributes a plant, distribution networks, and European market access.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: The direction of technology transfer in autos has flipped — Western OEMs are now the asset providers, which changes the negotiating leverage and the margin split.
insights.locator: The arrangement reflects a striking reversal of roles

insights.claim: The 1995 methanol coalition spanning Ford, the U.S. Energy Department, the National Science Foundation, MIT, Tsinghua University, Shanxi province, and industrial partners would be politically unthinkable today given far tenser U.S.-China relations.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: The collapse of U.S.-China research coupling is itself a cost — joint ventures in third countries are the workaround now available.
insights.quote: It was a coalition of governmental and nongovernmental, central and local, and technology and industry partners across the Pacific that would be politically unthinkable today in an era of far tenser U.S.-China relations.

insights.claim: The United States and Europe may be unable to reproduce the industrial ecosystems China built through decades of policy investment, making carefully structured technology partnerships the alternative route to fast-track technological learning at home.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: This reframes Western policy from reshoring to negotiated integration — a bullish case for JV structures over pure tariff-driven onshoring.

insights.claim: Partnership design determines whether technology is actually absorbed: political stakeholders demand deals tied to local production, workforce development, domestic suppliers, and shared research rather than import-and-assembly arrangements.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Screen announced China-West JVs on local-content and co-development terms — those without them will face political reversal risk.

insights.claim: The immediate benefits of the Valencia venture are higher utilization of Ford’s existing manufacturing assets, lower costs and reduced execution risk for Geely versus a greenfield European plant, and spillovers for Spain, Europe’s second-largest automobile producer.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Brownfield JVs beat greenfield for Chinese OEMs entering Europe on both cost and political acceptability — expect imitation.

insights.claim: At the heart of the venture is a new multi-energy family crossover launching in 2028 that Ford describes as designed by Ford and jointly developed with Geely, creating opportunities for genuine technological exchange including China’s cost-effective electrical/electronic architectures being used in U.S.-brand vehicles.
insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Chinese E/E architecture entering a U.S. brand is the specific capability transfer to watch — it is the main cost gap between Chinese and Western EVs.

insights.speaker: Lizzi C. Lee, Fengming Lu
insights.so_what: Technology programs used as relationship currency rarely survive commercial pressure — a caution when reading strategic partnership announcements.
